notes.title: Updated Campaign: Releasing the Beta
notes.content:
Content Update Beta begins today!


Attention Troopers!

Another major free content update is now LIVE on the Open Beta branch! This update brings new units, mission improvements, and performance improvements to the base game and both DLCs.

Note that all Territory Mode content has been disabled in this beta update, but expect another major update for this upcoming new game mode soon. Please see the bottom of this post if you want to access the old Territory Mode beta on a separate Steam branch.


Base game: New units & improvements
The Kwalasha campaign adds new units with unique roles. The M4A Grinder is a light weapons platform capable of delivering rapid fire. Two new bipeds - the M9A Sledgehammer, which carries a heavy mortar for long-range support, and the M6A Jaeger with its heavy anti-armor gun and spotter drone - provide new mobile firepower. And finally, the Fortis E-Pulse Troopers wear heavy armor suits for a strong frontline defense.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/df2752bb53039f0dddcf3ea1e7c455b098e98688.png"]


Raising Hell DLC: New units & improvements
New mercenary units and mission updates add versatile support to the field. The Drilling Biped is a rugged vehicle that repairs machines, builds defenses, and holds its own in close combat. The Hunter-Killer Merc is quite the opposite: delivering precise long-range strikes, aided by a companion drone for spotting and close support. Lastly, the Merc Squad has also been upgraded with varied weapons for greater adaptability.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/c5f5156ac6b8d5f860d68e6518a9cf4695ddc379.png"]


Urban Onslaught DLC: Improvements
Missions have been updated to feature the new units and the A-12 Pegasus gunship can now unleash relentless rocket barrages on designated areas on the ground.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/4cbdf831d2df3e08aac0cbb44823f44a3d98ab00.png"]



Many missions have been rebalanced or updated, integrating these new units in their respective campaigns. We recommend you start a new playthrough to get the best experience! 


Performance improvements
Significant optimizations alleviate the slowdown experienced during long play sessions and on larger maps, ensuring smoother gameplay across the board. However, this is still in Beta, and we are working on more improvements.


Note to our Map Makers
This update includes significant balance changes! If you're creating or maintaining custom maps, be sure to playtest your maps to ensure everything still plays as intended. 

We’ve also added a few new decorations—and we can’t wait to see how you’ll use them in your creative community maps!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/40b53a6d2e028de407ff5a35e4e06cccfd9dcdc9.png"]


How to join the Beta:
To participate in the beta program, go through the following steps:

Right click on Starship Troopers: Terran Command in your Steam Library

Click on Properties

Click on Betas

Click on drop-down menu and select "Beta - Open Beta"

Then Steam should automatically update the game and download the beta


Old Territory Mode Beta
To access the old Territory Mode beta, go through the following steps:

Right click on Starship Troopers: Terran Command in your Steam Library

Click on Properties

Click on Betas

Click on drop-down menu and select "beta-territory-4.1.1 - Territory Mode Old Beta"

Then Steam should automatically update the game and download the beta



We hope you will enjoy the new content and that you will use the new units to tear those Arachnids a new one!  Be sure to join our Discord server to report any bugs or issues that you encounter in this beta.

notes.title: New Roadmap - 3rd Anniversary Update
notes.content:
Troopers!

Next week, the 16h of June, is the third anniversary of Starship Troopers: Terran Command. To celebrate this - and to show you how we remain dedicated to supporting and expanding upon the game - we are sharing the year 4 roadmap today.

Without further ado, check the infographic below! But don’t stop there, as we go into more detail about its content further down in this post.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/6f88c3f2e1abd429b30349d1918a98ddda81013e.jpg"]
Campaign Update | Summer 2025
The first free update brings new content and improvements to the base game and both of the existing DLCs. New player units have been added to the Kwalasha campaign - and several are also available in the DLC campaigns. Many Kwalasha missions have also been updated to focus on these new units and to enhance the overall experience.

The Raising Hell DLC will also receive a small amount of new Mercenary unit types, along with significant improvements to its campaign missions. The Urban Onslaught campaign has additionally been updated with several changes to its missions, mostly focused on the new units.

In addition to all of the above, this update includes significant performance improvements, specifically targeting the slowdowns you may have experienced during long play sessions and on larger maps.

All this new content will be available in the Open Beta next month.


Territory Mode | Autumn 2025
If you’ve been following our Dev Diaries, you know we have a new game mode - Territory Mode - in development. It offers unprecedented freedom in unit selection and tactics. Played on new maps crafted specifically for Territory Mode, you’ll battle the Arachnids to capture Territory Points, adding a fresh strategic layer to the game.

The base game and each DLC will get exclusive Territory Mode maps and their own unique Battle Group. Please see our last Dev Diary for full details, but in short: a Battle Group comprises a tailored set of unit types, technologies and gameplay mechanics - several available only to that group.

Choose your Battle Group and challenge the Arachnids across countless generated mission variations!


First “Battle Group” DLC | End of 2025
At the end of the year, we’ll release a new type of DLC that is focused exclusively on Territory Mode. Fight the Bugs on several new Territory Mode maps set on a brand new planet, with its own unique environment and bringing several new Arachnid unit types. Unlike the currently available DLCs, no story campaign will be included in this DLC. Instead, you’ll gain exclusive access to a uniquely themed Battle Group featuring its own units, technologies and gameplay mechanics.


New “Story Campaign” DLC | Early 2026
Early next year another big “story campaign” DLC will drop. Similar in scope to the Raising Hell and Urban Onslaught DLCs, this will feature a brand new story campaign, set on a jungle planet and featuring new characters, new units and new Arachnids.

In addition to the campaign content, the DLC also expands Territory Mode with new maps and its own unique Battle Group - featuring the units available in the campaign, as well as new technologies and gameplay mechanics.




We hope you’re as excited as we are, Troopers - your war against the Bugs is only just getting started!

notes.title: Dev Diary #5: Territory Mode Battle Groups
notes.content:
Troopers! It’s about time for a big intel drop on the upcoming Territory Mode.

A lot of work is going into the new game mode behind the screens. In today’s Dev Diary we will delve deeper into the concept of Battle Groups, and how these form the core of the Territory Mode experience.

New modes, new menus
The introduction of the new game mode has necessitated a redesign of the main menu. We’ve already highlighted this in a previous Dev Diary, but further changes have been made based on player feedback and new design requirements.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/46241fa35c699fb6608dc1928a3c354ce859c6d5.png

When clicking the “GO TO WAR!” button, a new screen will require you to select a game mode: Story campaigns, challenge missions or Territory Mode.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/4cb6f4f2cebc278f3d692550e0f8fe95db4b2bbd.png

Battle Group selection
After entering Territory Mode, next you’ll be presented with the Battle Group selection screen. The base game and each DLC will come with its own Battle Group - each featuring a unique theme and set of exclusive units, mechanics and technologies. In this screen, you can also access a summarized information overview for each of the available Battle Groups.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/034c125c2e0b5bf7c5dc62af3540d3b0bd756fb9.png

Battle Group missions & progression
Choose your Battle Group and you’ll enter the “Mission Selection Screen”. In this screen, missions will be available for you to accept on Kwalasha - the base game’s planet - or any of the planets from the DLCs that you own. This means that, regardless of which Battle Group you have selected, you can fight in any environment and against all Arachnid unit types that the game and DLCs offer. As we continue to release new DLC, this variety will only expand.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/3bb11f8af0a53c14cd3272f19d5f4296e19457a9.png

Missions not only vary by planet, but also by starting tier, map type, objectives and Arachnid threats you’re expected to encounter.

The first time you start playing with a Battle Group, only a limited set of basic units and technologies will be available during the early missions. As you complete missions, however, you will unlock new unit types, new technologies and more complex, higher tier missions will become available. But beware, new Arachnid types and threats will also activate as you progress with the selected Battle Group.

Once you launch the selected mission, you’ll be taken into battle.

Playing a Mission
A quick summary about Territory Mode gameplay: you capture territory points to acquire resources over time. These can be used to deploy units, call for reinforcements and to acquire new technologies. Technologies provide access to new unit types or apply upgrades that expand the performance or abilities of your units. For more information, see our previously released Dev Diaries.

Each Battle Group has its own set of technologies and unit types. Some of these may be shared with other Battle Groups, but many are exclusive and thus offer unique challenges and gameplay experiences.

The following screenshots show the different content available to the “Ground Pounders” - available as part of the base game - and the “Hellraisers” - available with the Raising Hell DLC. Note that this content is still in development and may differ once the Territory Mode is officially released.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/84d160e423553d6e43d7c9ec891ecc6323591b0c.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/13f99f4b7eee3e280f42cc092295c3da5b94d8a8.png

The Technologies available during your mission depend on the mission's maximum Battle Tier, and is restricted to the content you have unlocked in the “Mission Selection Screen”.

If you manage to achieve all primary objectives - or fail a critical objective - the mission will end and you'll be taken back to the Mission Selection Screen. If a victory was achieved, new content may unlock. But regardless of the outcome, new generated missions will become available to choose - so you’ll always have new challenges ready to accept.

That’s all for now on Territory Mode, Trooper. For a final bit of news: Next month we’ll be announcing a new roadmap update - including still unannounced DLC content!

notes.title: Territory Mode - Dev Diary #3
notes.content:
Welcome back, Troopers!

It has been two months since we rolled out the Open Beta for Territory Mode, and over 10,000 of you have already joined the fight. We want to send a big thank-you to everyone who’s been battling the Arachnids and sending us invaluable feedback. Your reports from the frontlines continue to shape and improve Territory Mode.

We’re now focusing on making the mode easier to learn, refining difficulty, and adding more content. Meanwhile, we’re also working behind the scenes on our next DLC - but that’s a story for another day.

A Note from the Engineering Corps: Savegames
We’ve heard your requests, and our engineers have been hard at work behind the scenes to add savegame support for Territory Mode. This upgrade means you’ll be able to save your progress and pick up right where you left off - no more losing hours of hard-fought territory gains because a sneaky Tanker decided to pop out of nowhere! We know you’ll appreciate fewer “rough moments” on the road to crushing the Arachnids.

Turret Troubles and Triumphs
One of the recent changes in Territory Mode is how turrets now behave when destroyed by Bugs. Rather than exploding into a pile of scrap, they enter a “disabled mode”. Technicians, Engineers - or the fancy new repair drones, see below - can bring them back online, preserving any precious upgrades you invested in. Additionally, our artist is hard at work on improved visuals for these disabled turrets. You’ll be able to tell at a glance which turrets can be repaired and returned to combat readiness, making it easier than ever to rebuild your defensive line after a crushing Arachnid assault.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/bef035134fcc9eb8deafe1723108ab08f129d270.gif

New Turret upgrade: Repair Drone
In tandem with the turret visual improvements comes the Repair Drone - a nifty upgrade you can requisition for your Mortar Turret. Once unlocked, this flying friend will buzz around a radius, actively patching up damaged turrets. It’s the perfect backup when the frontlines are swarming and your Combat Engineers are busy clearing out Bug hives.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/326c1ccd72dd35f136b902919073635445e6a970.gif

More to Come
We’ve been flooded (in a good way!) with feedback and player data from your two months in the field, and there’s still more on the horizon. We can’t wait to share future updates, balance tweaks, and brand-new surprises as Territory Mode continues to evolve. Keep those reports coming, Troopers.

Haven’t joined the Open Beta yet? Suit up and help us refine Territory Mode into the best experience it can be. With every Bug squashed, every turret repaired, and every feedback form submitted, you’re helping the Federation stay one step ahead of the Arachnid threat.

Service guarantees citizenship. Now, get back out there and do your part!

notes.title: Territory Mode - Dev Diary #2
notes.content:
Welcome back, Troopers!

We’re excited to share some more insights on Territory Mode, the new game mode that will be released as part of a free update, next year.

Want to jump in early and help us develop this new game mode? Then sign up for the closed beta here!

https://www.slitherine.com/beta/starship-troopers-terran-command

A short recap:
Territory Mode is a new game mode specifically designed for replayability. A range of new maps has been created specifically for Territory Mode. In these maps, you can choose which units to use from the base game and from all DLCs that you own. For example, you can play with the Raising Hell DLC mercenaries against the new Bugs from the Urban Onslaught DLC.
In this game mode, Federation and Arachnid forces battle it out over Resource Points. These points reward the player with the necessary resources required to purchase units, replace casualties and invest in new technologies.
Now, let’s dive into another topic: the new and improved Arachnid AI, designed to test your tactical skills as you fight for every inch of territory.

Defenses and expansions
When you start a new Territory Mode map, it will be crawling with Arachnids that won’t surrender their territory without a fight. While you expand your territory, the Bugs will try to retake it from nearby areas. If your defenses are poorly placed, the Bugs will outflank you and pierce through your territory.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/2c675585005d38c7c9a03d507294873538b89697.gif

The more territory points you capture, the more paths the Bugs have to attack your territory. To hold the Arachnids at bay, you can rely on the multiple turret types provided by the Federation.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/1c0d42a3bd3971345f19e9b10a226d0cb9b3cf57.gif

To keep the endless flow of Arachnid attacks on your territory running, the Bugs constantly reinforce their own territory from hives. Fed Intel has confirmed that clearing out all the hives in an area will neutralize the Arachnid threat.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/910bf937cb3f084a7bb4fb8d30be37caa48dd03f.gif

Arachnid World Events
While the Arachnids often rely on overwhelming the MI in head-to-head combat, they do have other tricks up their sleeves. (do Bugs have sleeves?)
A new tactic they have: While the MI is hard at work on the frontline, pushing forward and claiming territory, the Bugs will sneakily burrow through the ground to attack your back line. Make sure to keep some back up defenses and turrets in your territory!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/51d29b02b23734ce327f5cd56201dfb8b4fbb211.gif

This is only one of the many new fighting styles the Bugs have. Which events you will encounter will differ every time you start a new territory map, so you’ll have to decide which units and technologies to invest in. This offers a different challenge each time you play.
That’s all for this update. We can't wait to see how you will counter these new Arachnid threats. Stay tuned in the coming weeks for more information!

notes.title: DLC sneak peek: Turret defenses
notes.content:
Greetings, Troopers,

In this update, we’ll provide a quick overview of the new turrets available in the upcoming Urban Onslaught DLC, along with a new resource type for acquiring these new units. Also, Closed Beta signups for the Urban Onslaught DLC are still open, if you are interested in giving feedback on the upcoming DLC you can still sign up!

JOIN THE BETA HERE

The Federation has provided access to a new line of advanced defensive turrets due to the increased Arachnid threat facing the great city of Mahanagar. Because each turret type has its own strengths and weaknesses, it is crucial to find the right mix and position them correctly to repel the Bug attack waves.

Autocannon & Mortar Turrets
The Autocannon Turret is designed for engaging medium-armored and airborne enemies. It has good armor and high hitpoints, providing an excellent frontline barrier. But keep in mind that while this turret can fire over infantry units and most other turrets, it cannot fire over elevations or tall obstacles. Also, its efficiency decreases when engaging numerous targets due to the cannons overheating fairly quickly.
The Mortar Turret is designed to complement the Autocannon Turret, as it excels against masses of unarmored enemies with its large area of effect. It has indirect fire, allowing it to lob projectiles over both units and terrain elevations. However, the Mortar Turret projectiles are slow-moving, and the turret has a significant minimum range, making it ineffective against fast-moving targets and more vulnerable to direct attacks. 
Together, these two turret types provide a balanced defense against a wide range of lower tier Bug types.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/b7f3b489d38eb814196de16a30a8c203fffe5dcc.gif

Heavy Gun Turret & Sentry Turret
The Heavy Gun Turret has a large cannon that fires projectiles capable of piercing even the most heavily armored Arachnids. The turret's drawbacks include a fairly slow reload time and slow rotation speed, which hinders its effectiveness against large numbers of enemies and fast moving targets.
The new Riot Shield Squad unit has the ability to launch a container that deploys a “Sentry Turret”. These small turrets operate autonomously and cannot be controlled directly by the player. They provide temporary, automated fire support, but expire after a short duration, making them ideal for creating brief strategic advantages during intense combat situations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/ae0be3fcc65e36cc9396a3c5d99c6750fb818015.gif

Ballistic Missile Turret
Optimized for long-range engagements, the Ballistic Missile Turret boasts an impressive range and fires armor-piercing missiles. These missiles feature a built-in homing system that increases the likelihood of hitting moving targets. The turret is designed specifically for taking out hard-to-reach priority targets, as its very slow reload time makes it virtually useless in direct confrontations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/66287050460db89b850f711806ff3578e9300bc6.gif

New Resource: Materiel
To acquire these advanced defensive units, a new resource type  has been introduced. This resource, called Materiel, is used for buying mechanical units and turrets. It regenerates slowly after losing units that require this resource, meaning frequent losses could cause significant delays in restocking and redeployment.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/efe5b91d20a4550f9d4816a4e8e1f306db10d97a.gif

The Closed Beta for our Urban Onslaught DLC is still running. If you're eager to experience the new content first-hand and help shape its development, this is your chance! Sign up for the closed beta here.

That’s all for this update. We are certain that these new turrets will make you feel safer while defending your neighborhood. Lets just hope there is no Brain Bug present...

notes.title: 3 New Challenge Missions for Raising Hell DLC
notes.content:
Three new challenge missions for the Raising Hell DLC are currently in development. Owners of the DLC can already play them on the Open Beta branch. Scroll to the bottom of this post for more information on how to gain access.

Mission: Prospect & Protect

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/da63daa50db2d13be825d84eb5ca72a5b2aaf105.png

The main objective in this scenario is to gather soil samples at various locations by constructing and defending “prospectors”. In order to achieve this, you’ll have to muster a force of mercenaries in your outpost base and venture down into Bug territory.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/7311703e4b51dd5053b153bddf4877aa3d0e926e.png

At the same time, however, relentless Arachnid attack waves are pouring in from the opposite side of the outpost. Losing it will result in certain defeat, so while your expeditionary force takes care of the prospectors, other units must be assigned to defend the wall.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/28a98ea97c437b123d5b2eb699285b98b48e2fea.png

The scenario provides an excellent opportunity to experiment with various compositions of all the new mercenary unit types, both in an offensive and defensive role.

Your final score will be based on how long you managed to survive against the ever increasing attack waves, as well as the amount of hives and nests cleared in Arachnid territory.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36290235/af99218de55b21994fb2dd0ecdadede8a91c4764.png

While your starting base is important for the deployment of new units and infrastructure, the terrain offers various treacherous routes between Bug hives and additional Radio Stations. It is up to you to determine how to best approach the situation.

Adding to the challenge, an imminent ash storm threatens to impede reinforcements. Radio Stations sporadically dot the map, but time is scarce, and troops are limited to secure them for an extended duration.

Chemical Reaction Update

After a period in Open Beta, we are releasing the Chemical Reaction Update for everyone.

Containing three new scenarios, one new unit type and the target priority setting, this is the largest free update so far.

[previewyoutube=tQwoYBw5S7c;full][/previewyoutube]

Let's have a look at its content:

- Three new scenarios, two of which make use of the first incarnation of a new high-score system;
- One new unit type: Chemical Troopers; this unit is currently only available in the new scenarios, but there are plans to include it in future content as well. It's a squad of expert troopers using biochemical weapons, which they use to great effect for exterminating anything with more than two legs;
- The Target Priority setting (TPS); units can be set to prioritize firing at specific enemy types instead of aiming for the nearest target. For instance, if you want to automatically target Spitter Bugs with your Snipers, TPS allows you to avoid that level of micromanagement.

You can find the full changelog here.

Chemical Reaction

notes.title: Starship Troopers: Terran Command - Update v1.8.0
notes.content:
Greetings Troopers,

today we are releasing a new update. It is a fixes and balance changes update, and among others we are fixing the issue that made players having Turkish as their system language crash. We apologize for the issue, it should be fixed now.

We are aware that there are concerns about the spawn rate of the Scorpion Bugs, we are looking into solutions on how to best tackle that.

Please, let us know your feedback and opinions. We intend to further improve Starship Troopers: Terran Command and your feedback is very helpful for us to make it happen. 

In the meantime, work continues... we have plans for future content and features, and we're just about to finalize them. We'll be back soon with an actual Roadmap containing information on what's next.

Full Changelog:

- Wiki: Entry and popup added for elite abilities.
- Added cap to amount of Auto Saves of 50.
Fixes:
- Fixed crash for Turkish and Azerbaijani Windows users.
- Localisation: fixed unit name tooltips not properly translated.
- Operation Guillotine: Fixed issue when capturing the middle Radio Station before clearing the initial hives.
- Difficulty modifier no longer affects damage of allied units.
Balance changes:
- Tanker armor reduced from 120 to 100
- Scorpion armor reduced from 90 to 70
- Scorpion range reduced from 35 to 30
- Scorpion Armor-Piercing (AP) reduced from 80 to 60
- Rocket Trooper range reduced from 45 to 35
- Rifle Squad Armor-Piercing (AP) reduced
- Marauder primary weapon AP reduced
- Marauder Mortar Barrage accuracy increased, damage and blast radius reduced
- Marauder Drop Charge damage doubled
- Spitter AP increased from 0 to 40
- "Suppression Resistant" units can only be slowed by 50% instead of 70%
Settings:
- Removed option to disable "runInBackground" as it is suspected to cause GFX issues.
- Removed screen refresh rate selection as it is not properly supported.
- Game will no longer cap framerate to 60fps when vsync is off, instead it will use the screen's current refresh rate as cap.
- Fixed resolution reset when changing refresh rate.
- Hotfix for setting refresh rates for some machines, still being investigated.
Known issues:
 - Scorpion spawning rate is not balanced, we are still investigating the best way to fix the spawning rules.
